title: §08-003: Package Management, Module Isolation & ESM Interop
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §08-003 (Package Management, Module Isolation & ESM Interop).

cards.concept: Package Management, Module Isolation & ESM Interop: CommonJS vs ESM Live Bindings
cards.question: What is the key difference between CommonJS exports and ECMAScript Module (ESM) exports regarding exported variables?

options.text: CommonJS exports live bindings, whereas ESM creates an immutable deep copy of module.exports.
ESM exports live read-only bindings that reflect mutations in the exporting module dynamically; CommonJS exports a copied snapshot of module.exports.
ESM requires all modules to be compiled into binary bytecode first.
CommonJS allows top-level await in all files by default.

cards.explanation: ESM creates live bindings: when a variable in an exporting module changes, all importing modules observe the updated value. CommonJS copies values onto module.exports at execution time.
cards.pitfall: Attempting to reassign an imported binding (e.g. count = 2) in ESM throws TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.

cards.concept: Package Management, Module Isolation & ESM Interop: Dual-Package Hazard in Node.js
cards.question: What is the 'dual-package hazard' in Node.js package development, and how is it resolved in `package.json`?

options.text: Publishing a package with both JavaScript and TypeScript source files in the same folder.
When an application loads both CJS and ESM builds of the same package, causing singletons and instance checks (instanceof) to be duplicated and desynchronized.
Exceeding the npm 100MB compressed package upload limit.
Using npm and bun simultaneously in the same repo.

cards.explanation: If a package provides both CJS and ESM entry points without proper wrapping, two separate module instances are loaded into memory, breaking singletons and instanceof checks.
cards.pitfall: Maintaining package state in module variables when both CJS and ESM entry points are bundled without a shared state wrapper.
cards.citation: Node.js Packages Guide: Dual CommonJS/ES Module Packages
